This Trade Score aggregates human emotion (Fear & Greed, Put/Call Ratios) and mathematical over-extensions (RSI, SMA Distance) into a single 0–100 value to detect market capitulation.
The higher the score, the better the buying opportunity because the crowd is panicking. The lower the score, the higher the risk of a severe pullback because the crowd is euphoric and greedy.
This is the algorithmic system\'s direct recommendation on whether you should be buying the dip, holding your ground, or trimming your profits today.

The Investor Score is calculated as a weighted average of Trend, Health, and Risk. A score > 65 indicates a confirmed, healthy Bull Market supported by strong economic plumbing. A score < 45 indicates a Bear Market or a severe, dangerous correction.

This Risk Score is a blended macroeconomic aggregate measuring hidden systemic stress. It analyzes bond volatility, yield curve inversions, credit spreads, and institutional asset rotation.

Note: The model includes a \'Contagion Penalty\'. If any single gauge flashes extreme danger, the overall score is automatically pushed higher to reflect the risk of market contagion, even if other areas appear calm.

Risk Assessment is an AI-identified list of potential risks that could derail the current market narrative, each scored by potential impact and explained against today\'s macro regime. It refreshes several times a day and closes with a one-sentence read on overall market fragility. This describes potential threats, not a forecast or recommendation. This interpretation is generated by an AI model and may not reflect current market conditions.

The Weekly Playbook is an AI-curated shortlist of the economic releases most likely to move markets this week, drawn from the upcoming economic calendar and regenerated every Sunday. Each event\'s context explains how it could confirm or challenge the current macro outlook; actual figures and their market impact are added mid-week as each release happens. This is scheduling context, not a trading signal or recommendation. This interpretation is generated by an AI model and may not reflect current market conditions.

Short-term sentiment and momentum readings — the Fear & Greed Index, Put/Call ratio, VIX, RSI, and how far price has stretched from its own moving average — the kind of signals that can shift meaningfully day to day. Extremes in either direction have historically preceded a reversal, but they describe current conditions, not a prediction of what happens next.

Broader measures of financial-system stress and risk appetite — the yield curve, credit spreads, market volatility (the MOVE index), the dollar, oil, and cross-asset signals like the copper/gold ratio and market breadth. These tend to move more slowly than Tactical Momentum\'s readings, and widening stress here has historically been an early warning rather than a same-day signal.

How expensive or cheap the market looks relative to earnings, book value, and its own history — the P/E and P/B ratios, the equity risk premium, and dividend yield. A stretched valuation says the market is pricing in a lot of optimism, not that a decline is imminent — valuations can stay expensive (or cheap) for a long time.

The broader economic backdrop — inflation (CPI, core PCE), employment, and GDP growth — that shapes the Fed\'s policy path and the market\'s medium-term direction. These update on a monthly or quarterly cadence, so they move slower than the other three pillars.

Market Pulse is a research tool for investors who want to understand what the market is doing — not be told what to do about it. It aggregates real market data, macro indicators, and company fundamentals, runs them through deterministic analysis, and surfaces the results alongside AI-written interpretation.\n\nWe name what the market is doing. What you do about it is yours.

Every number in the app — prices, ratios, chart values, gauge readings — is computed in code from real data sources before any AI touches it. AI is used only to write the interpretive text on top of those numbers: summaries, digests, narrative reads. The numbers and the words have different origins and different reliability profiles.\n\nData refreshes on a schedule, not continuously. Most indicators update once or a few times a day; a small set of live prices update every minute during market hours.

AI-written content is labeled \"AI-generated · Not advice\" everywhere it appears. Before any AI-written text is shown, it\'s automatically checked for advice-sounding language — if flagged, it\'s removed rather than shown. AI never invents a number; it only writes about numbers that were already computed.\n\nAI can still be wrong. It can misread data, overstate confidence, or miss context. Cross-check anything that would influence a real decision.

Market Pulse collects two kinds of data:

How you use the app — which screens you visit, what you tap, how you engage. This is standard app-analytics data (via Firebase Analytics), tied to an anonymous app-install ID, not to you as a person. No name, no email, no account.

Crash reports — if the app crashes, a technical report is sent automatically including device model and OS version, used only to fix defects (via Firebase Crashlytics).

• No account or sign-in exists — we have no way to identify you.
• No financial account, brokerage, or payment information.
• No location data.
• No data from the market sources you view — those are fetched by our servers, never by your device directly.
Your theme, favorited stocks and metrics, and app settings are stored only on your device. They leave your device only if you back up your device yourself. Uninstalling the app removes them.

The market data you see comes from third-party providers (Finnhub, Yahoo Finance, FRED, and others). Those providers never receive information about you or your device — all data fetching happens server-side.

If you turn on notifications, your device subscribes to anonymous topics, such as the daily summary or stock analysis updates. Delivery runs through Google\'s Firebase Cloud Messaging. Market Pulse doesn\'t link a subscription to you, keeps no list of subscribed devices, and has no way to send a notification to one person. Turning a notification off in Settings unsubscribes the device.

Short-term yields above long-term = inverted — historically an early recession warning.
Price stretched more than +10% above its 200-day average, or more than -5% below it, tends to mean-revert — though a strong trend can stay stretched for a while.

Different scales, same idea: market mood. Extremes are the most informative reading and can persist for weeks. Fear & Greed and Put/Call both read contrarian — and Put/Call\'s scale runs the opposite direction of the other two, so \"more fearful\" is to the left here, not the right.
Illustrative values, not live data — see the real gauge inside the app for today\'s actual reading.

Read contrarian: extreme fear has historically coincided with periods where selling pressure was overdone, extreme greed with periods of elevated risk-taking. Neither is a timing signal on its own — both can stay at an extreme for a long time.
Reads the same way, in reverse: a high ratio means heavy put-buying (fear), a low ratio means heavy call-buying (greed). Just as capable of sitting at an extreme for weeks without anything changing.
Most useful ranked against its own recent history, not as a raw number alone — extremes in either direction have historically preceded a reversal as crowded positioning unwinds.

A widely watched but famously unreliable contrarian indicator on its own: extreme readings are sometimes read as a sign a consensus view has gotten crowded, not as confirmation that the consensus is right.
Overbought — momentum may be due for a pause, not a reversal call.

Every gauge and indicator across Market Pulse follows the same idea: a raw value gets bucketed into a plain-language read (e.g. \"Extreme Fear,\" \"Overbought,\" \"Neutral\") using thresholds defined elsewhere, not judged case by case. The definitions below come from the same glossary data the rest of the app uses — tap any gauge in the app itself for the fuller breakdown, including its current band and any gotchas specific to that metric.\n\nSome of these you can check yourself: the yield curve, RSI, and a stock\'s P/E versus its sector are standard measures you\'ll find on any financial site — use them to test what the app is showing you. Others, like the Fear & Greed Index or this app\'s own Copper/Gold ratio, are composite reads you can\'t easily rebuild from raw data — treat those as one lens, not gospel. Either way, the app names the condition; the conclusion is yours to draw.

Positioning shows where retail sentiment (AAII), large speculators (CFTC COT futures positioning), and short sellers (FINRA short interest) currently stand — three different lenses on who\'s leaning which way. A crowded reading in either direction has historically preceded a reversal as that positioning unwinds. None of these are predictions or recommendations; they describe current positioning, which can shift or reverse without warning. This interpretation is generated by an AI model and may not reflect current market conditions.

Posture tracks how professional money managers, institutional order flow, and system-wide liquidity are positioned beneath the surface of daily price moves — active manager equity exposure (NAAIM), dark pool accumulation (DIX), and the Fed\'s net liquidity backdrop. Like Positioning, this describes current conditions, not a forecast or recommendation. This interpretation is generated by an AI model and may not reflect current market conditions.
Tracks the average equity exposure of active money managers. 0% represents cash/short, 100% is fully invested, and >100% indicates leveraged long positioning.
% of dark pool volume, institutional buying
Measures the percentage of total dark pool volume that was institutional buying. A reading above 45% suggests heavy institutional accumulation under the surface.
Fed balance sheet − TGA − reverse repo
Calculates the actual fiat liquidity flowing through the financial system. Rising liquidity generally acts as a tailwind for equities and crypto, while falling liquidity acts as a headwind.

Weekly AAII survey of individual investor sentiment. The bull-bear spread is a classic contrarian indicator — extreme optimism or pessimism among retail investors has historically preceded a reversal.

Speculative net futures positioning as a percentage of open interest, framed against a trailing ~1-year percentile per contract. A crowded long or short reading has historically preceded a reversal as that positioning unwinds — first-pass framing, not backtested. Reflects the prior Tuesday\'s book, not the report\'s Friday release date. ES/NQ/RTY use CFTC\'s Legacy non-commercial category; DIA uses TFF\'s Leveraged Funds category instead (Dow futures aren\'t reported under Legacy) — see each contract\'s own methodology before comparing DIA directly against the other three.

FINRA-reported short interest in SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA/RSP/MAGS as index/style-ETF proxies — not literal \'market short interest.\' Includes authorized-participant creation/redemption arbitrage flow, not purely directional bearish positioning. Settlement-date data, always roughly 8 business days stale by the time FINRA publishes it (see each instrument\'s settlement date vs. this gauge\'s fetched-at time).

A snapshot of the whole market: today\'s AI-written digest, sentiment gauges, futures, and your tracked assets, all in one scrollable feed.

Numbers, charts, and prices are computed directly from data — no AI involved.

• Daily Digest: generated by AI from today's top market-moving stories and price action across major indices, updated once per trading day. The one AI-written section on this screen, labeled "AI-generated · Not advice."
• Gauges (Fear & Greed, Put/Call Ratio, etc.): show where a reading currently sits on its own scale — the colored band tells you which zone it's in, not what to do about it.

Every tracked indicator grouped into four pillars — Tactical Momentum, Systemic Risk, Valuation, and Macro Vitals — plus a cross-pillar AI read at the top and a Horizons view of how it plays out over time.

Each pillar's summary (Tactical Momentum, Systemic Risk, Valuation, Macro Vitals) is generated by AI, based on that pillar's own underlying computed values, to explain what they mean together and what to watch across different time horizons. Only that explanatory text is AI-written — the values themselves are computed directly from data.

• AGREEMENT and STANCE pills: computed directly from data, not AI-judged.
• Metric cards: a raw value plus a plain-language status (e.g. NEUTRAL, OVERSOLD) based on fixed thresholds, not a model's opinion.

A single day\'s market briefing, built from this app\'s own data. Swipe between days or tap a date to see that day\'s Market Signal, Market Sentiment, and Drivers, plus Market Movers, Macro Mix, The Domino Effect, What to Watch, and Risks to Market. The latest report also shows Market Position and What\'s New.

• Market Signal: the risk-on/risk-off direction is derived in code from this app's indicators; the regime label, the headline, and the Market Read text are AI-written from that same data. Tap the headline for the fuller read.
• Market Sentiment: an AI-written read of the Posture and Positioning gauges — tap it to open them.
• Drivers: what the report ties the day's tone to. Tap Show Indicators to see the underlying gauges.
• Market Movers, Macro Mix, The Domino Effect, What to Watch, and Risks to Market: AI-written narrative that describes conditions and possible chains of events — not predictions of how the market will react.
• Everything AI-written on this screen is labeled "AI-generated · Not advice" at the bottom of the page.
Four tabs — Events (Weekly Playbook), Risks, Posture, and Positioning — each pairing a deterministic gauge with an AI-written synthesis of what it currently shows.

Every tab follows the same shape: computed gauges and data cards first, then one AI-written summary card below them, labeled "AI-generated · Not advice."

• Events (Weekly Playbook): the scheduled economic releases most likely to move markets this week — context on what each could signal, not a prediction of the reaction.
• Risks: a curated list of what could derail the current narrative, each scored by potential impact.
• Posture: how professional money is positioned beneath the surface — active-manager exposure (NAAIM), dark-pool accumulation (DIX), and system-wide liquidity.
• Positioning: where three different crowds stand — retail sentiment (AAII), large speculators (CFTC futures), and short sellers (FINRA).

A crowded reading in either direction is worth noticing: extremes have historically preceded reversals as that positioning unwinds — but "crowded" can stay crowded for a while. The app names where things stand; what you make of it is yours.
Tracked stocks, indices, and ETFs with a live price, a short AI-written read of their technical setup, and status pills (e.g. Overbought, Undervalued) computed from this app\'s own data.

• Status pills (RANGE BOUND, Undervalued, etc.): computed directly from price/fundamental data using fixed rules.\n• The read above them: generated by AI from the symbol\'s price trend, moving averages, volume, and valuation data, updated after each trading session — the one AI-written element on each card.\n• Deep Dive (inside a symbol\'s detail screen): a longer AI-written breakdown, generated roughly every two weeks or sooner around earnings, from an expanded set of price, fundamental, and macro-context data.
